description:
List the contracts and insurance policies Well read from the workspace's documents, each contract with the notice date its own terms give and the supplier it is with. It draws no card. It answers when a contract renews or ends, when notice is due, and what an insurance policy covers and costs.

Each reading is the newest stored extraction of one document, never a register. The server applies the date arithmetic and the supplier match, and `as_of` is the day every `*_passed` flag was computed against. Pass `company_ids` (supplier `company_id` values) to match each reading to at most one of them.

Each contract carries `notice.status`:
  - `notice_deadline`: the contract renews automatically and `notice.deadline` (the end date minus the notice period) is the last day to give notice. `notice.deadline_passed` says whether that day is past.
  - `renews_automatically_next_unknown`: the contract renews automatically and its end date is past. The next end date is not on file.
  - `ends_on`: the reading states that the contract does not renew, so it ends on `end_date` and has no notice deadline. `notice.end_date_passed` says whether that day is past.
  - `renewal_unknown`: the reading does not state whether the contract renews. `notice.deadline` is `null`; `end_date` and `notice_period_days` are as stored.
  - `notice_period_unknown`: the contract renews automatically and ends today or later, but the reading holds no usable notice period.
  - `end_date_unknown`: the reading holds no usable end date.

`supplier.status: "matched"` means the contract's other party is the one supplier, among the `company_ids` passed, named by `supplier.company_id`; the match uses tax ids and email or website domains, never names. `unmatched` means no passed supplier was matched, and `supplier.reason` says why: `no_supplier_named` (no `company_ids` passed), `no_party_key` (the other party carries no tax id, email or website), `no_candidate` (no passed supplier shares a key with it) or `several_candidates` (more than one does, so none is chosen). `other_party_names` holds the names the reading prints for the parties that are not the workspace's own, for display only. `readable: false` means the stored reading did not parse: every term is `null` or unknown.

`insurance_policies` lists the insurance readings with the insurer, the policy type, the cover dates, the premium and its frequency, the sum insured and the deductible, each `null` when not read.

At most 50 readings, newest first; `readings_truncated: true` means older readings were not read. `partial: true` means the read was cut short and nothing was read. `unreadable_readings` counts the readings that did not parse. `unknown_company_ids` lists passed ids this workspace cannot read, so no contract was checked for them. `unkeyed_company_ids` lists readable suppliers that carry no tax id and no domain, so no contract can be tied to them. Non-disclosure agreements are never listed.

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no other tool call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

company_ids.description: The supplier company ids to match each reading against, at most 50. Omit to list the readings with no match.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several: this read reports one workspace's own figures and will not choose which.

name: well_list_contract_terms

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

resolved_workspace.description: The workspace that answered, when the caller named none and the token authorizes several.
